summary: A Devi shrine on a broad rocky river in Dang's north-west — quiet most of the year, a living centre of the district's adivasi devotion on its fair days.
description:
Mayadevi's temple sits in the forest-and-field country of north-western Dang, between the Waghai belt and the Subir falls cluster. Like most of the district's shrines it runs on two clocks: village-quiet through the ordinary year, and thronged when its fair days come around, when the goddess's following across the surrounding hamlets converges in the way Dang's adivasi devotion does — loud, musical and brief.

For travellers it works as the cultural stop on a western-interior loop — Mayadevi, then the Bhalkhet–Milan falls country east of it — and as a reminder that the district's living religion is its own attraction, distinct from the Ramayana geography of the Shabari sites.
highlights: A working Devi shrine of the district's adivasi tradition
Fair days transform the quiet forest temple
Pairs with the Subir falls belt for a western-interior day
history_legend: The shrine belongs to Dang's living goddess tradition; its fair gathers the surrounding villages. Details of the temple's founding and fair calendar need local verification.

modes.road: Village roads north-east from the Waghai side; ask for the Mayadevi mandir
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Short approach from the village road
access.road_condition: Rural tar; fine outside heavy rain

visit.notes: Fair days bring the year's crowds; otherwise a quiet darshan stop.

seasonality.notes: Comfortable post-monsoon through spring; check locally for fair dates.

experience.photography_notes: Ask before photographing worship — this is a living shrine, not a monument.

amenities.food: Village stalls on fair days; otherwise carry your own

warnings: Fair days mean dense crowds on narrow village roads — park early and walk

tips: Combine with the Bhalkhet–Milan falls belt east of the shrine in monsoon
If you can time a fair day, do — it is the temple's real life
